questions.stem: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Finance Commission of India established?
questions.explanation: Article 280 provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission. Article 263 covers the Inter-State Council; Article 324 deals with the Election Commission; Article 350 concerns language rights. The Finance Commission is a CONSTITUTIONAL body — constituted by the President every 5 years (or earlier if needed).
questions.subject: Polity

options.option_text: The Parliament through a special law
The Union Finance Minister after NITI Aayog approval

questions.explanation: Article 280(1): The President constitutes the Finance Commission every 5 years or at such earlier time as he considers necessary. The commission consists of a chairman and four other members. The PM/FM/NITI Aayog have no role in constitution — the function is squarely with the President (acting on Cabinet advice).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: How many members does the Finance Commission have?

options.option_text: Variable, determined by the Parliament each term

questions.explanation: Article 280(1): 'a Finance Commission which shall consist of a Chairman and four other Members'. The Finance Commission Act, 1951 lays down qualifications for appointment of members. Chairman is usually a person with public-affairs experience; members include a HC-eligible person, a finance expert, a public finance specialist, and an economics expert.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Finance Commission under Article 280?

options.option_text: Distribution of net proceeds of taxes between Union and States
Principles governing grants-in-aid to States out of the Consolidated Fund of India
Recommendations to augment Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement resources of Panchayats & Municipalities

questions.explanation: Article 280(3) lists functions: (a) distribution of tax proceeds between Union and States; (b) principles for grants-in-aid; (c) measures to augment State Consolidated Fund for local bodies (added by 73rd & 74th Amendments); (d) any other matter referred by the President. MSP for agricultural commodities is fixed by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on CACP recommendation — not the Finance Commission's role.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Who was the chairman of the First Finance Commission of India, constituted in 1951?
questions.explanation: K. C. Neogy chaired the First Finance Commission (1951–57). He was a senior economist and political leader. K. Santhanam chaired the 2nd FC (1956–62). Y. B. Chavan chaired the 8th FC (1984–89). Brahmanand Reddy never chaired an FC. The First FC's tenure covered April 1952 to March 1957.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which Finance Commission introduced the concept of 'performance-based grants' for local bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities)?
questions.explanation: The 13th FC (Chairman: Dr. Vijay Kelkar, 2010–15) was the first to introduce performance-based grants for local bodies, conditional on compliance with e.g., putting up audited accounts and establishing a local-level grievance redressal system. Earlier FCs (11th & 12th) gave only basic grants to local bodies. The 14th & 15th FCs continued the performance-grant structure with updated conditions.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which Finance Commission increased the States' share in the divisible pool of central taxes from 32% to 42%?
questions.explanation: The 14th FC (Chairman: Dr. Y. V. Reddy, covering 2015–20) made a landmark recommendation raising States' share of divisible central taxes from 32% (under the 13th FC) to 42% — the single largest jump in FC history, reflecting a new commitment to fiscal federalism. The 15th FC (N. K. Singh) slightly reduced it to 41% (on account of the J&K reorganisation into UTs).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: What is the usual tenure of a Finance Commission's recommendations?
questions.explanation: The Finance Commission is constituted every 5 years and its recommendations apply for the following 5-year period. E.g., 15th FC's recommendations covered 2021–26 (extended by 1 year due to COVID). This 5-year horizon matches the typical economic/planning cycle. The FC is NOT a permanent body; it is constituted afresh each time.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The recommendations of the Finance Commission are:

options.option_text: Binding on the Government of India
Advisory / recommendatory in nature; the government can modify or reject them
Binding on States but advisory for the Union

questions.explanation: The FC's recommendations are purely ADVISORY (Article 281). The President places the report before both Houses of Parliament along with an Explanatory Memorandum stating the government's action taken on each recommendation. The government can partially or fully reject recommendations — though in practice, the major recommendations (vertical devolution %, horizontal formula) are accepted. A famous case: the 14th FC raised devolution to 42%, which was fully accepted.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following criteria has been used by Finance Commissions for horizontal distribution (inter-State distribution) of tax proceeds?

options.option_text: Income distance, population, area, forest & ecology, demographic performance, and tax & fiscal efforts
GDP growth rate of each State only
Only population and tax collection capacity
Number of Lok Sabha seats held by each State

questions.explanation: Horizontal devolution uses multiple criteria with different weights. The 15th FC used: Income distance (45%), Area (15%), Population 2011 (15%), Demographic Performance (12.5%), Forest & Ecology (10%), Tax & Fiscal Efforts (2.5%). Earlier FCs had different weights and slightly different criteria (e.g., the 14th FC didn't use Forest & Ecology or Demographic Performance). The formula is designed to balance equity (give more to poorer States) and efficiency.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the State Finance Commission (constituted by the Governor every 5 years)?
questions.explanation: The State Finance Commission is a STATE-level body constituted by the Governor under Article 243-I (for Panchayats) AND Article 243-Y (for Municipalities) — both added by the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments (1992). It reviews the financial position of local bodies every 5 years and recommends distribution of State taxes. Article 280 is for the UNION FC, not the State FC.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Who chaired the 15th Finance Commission, whose recommendations cover the period 2021–2026?
questions.explanation: Nand Kishore Singh (N. K. Singh), former IAS officer and Chairman of the FRBM Review Committee, chaired the 15th FC (2017–21, report period 2021–26). Dr. Y. V. Reddy chaired the 14th FC; Dr. C. Rangarajan chaired the 12th FC (2005–10); Dr. Vijay Kelkar chaired the 13th FC.
